question: The difference between the selling prices of an article sold at a discount of 14 (1)/(2) \% and 10 (1)/(2) \% is 48. If the marked price is 25% more than the cost price, then the cost price of the article is:
solution:
**Given:**

The difference between the SPs of article sold at a discount of 14 (1)/(2) \% and 10 (1)/(2) \% is 48

MP is 25% more than the CP

Formula Used:

SP = MP × [(100 - Discount%)/100]

Calculation:

SP for 14 (1)/(2) \% discount = MP × (100% - 14.5%) = 85.5% of MP

SP for 10 (1)/(2) \% discount = MP × (100% - 10.5%) = 89.5% of MP

The difference between the discounts offered

⇒ 89.5% of MP - 85.5% of MP = 4% of MP

According to the question

4% of MP = 48

⇒ MP = 48 × (100/4) = ₹1200

CP when MP is 25 % more = 100over 125 × 1200 = ₹960

∴ The CP of the article is **₹**960.
